notes.meaning: Saul had just returned from driving away Philistine raiders when informants told him that David was hiding in the desert of En-gedi. En-gedi was a rocky oasis near the Dead Sea with many cliffs and large caves. Saul was so obsessed with destroying David that he immediately went back to hunting him without resting.

Saul gathered three thousand of the finest soldiers from all Israel to hunt David among the steep cliffs known as the Rocks of the Wild Goats. Bringing such a large army showed that Saul treated David like a dangerous enemy general. His blind rage drove him into craggy, dangerous ground where wild mountain goats lived.

Saul stopped by some stone sheep shelters along the road and went into a large cave, unaware that David and his men were hiding deep in the back. A person walking in from bright daylight could see nothing inside, while those already inside the dark cave could see clearly. God's quiet control over events brought the king completely into David's reach.

David's men urged him to strike, claiming this was the very day God had promised to hand Saul over to him. David crept forward quietly, but he only sliced off a corner of Saul's robe. He knew God had promised him the throne, but God had never given him permission to murder the king.

Right after cutting the cloth, David felt deep guilt in his heart. Even though he had not harmed Saul's body, he realized that damaging the king's royal robe was an act of disrespect toward God's ruler. A tender conscience will alert us even to small wrongs so we do not commit greater sins.

David told his men that the Lord strictly forbade him from harming his master, because Saul was the Lord's anointed. To be anointed meant God had specially chosen and consecrated him as king with holy oil. David knew it was God's job, not his own, to remove an unworthy ruler.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that David reverenced the sacred mystery of anointing itself, which remained holy in Saul despite his personal sins.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that 'touch not the Lord's anointed' means church members must never question, evaluate, or openly criticize their pastors and leaders.

notes.meaning: David used firm words to restrain his men and refused to let them harm Saul. Saul then walked out of the cave unharmed and continued on his way. David not only refused to do wrong himself, but he also made sure those under his command did no evil.

David came out of the cave and called out after Saul, saying, 'My lord the king!' When Saul turned around, David bowed low with his face to the dirt to show royal honor. By stepping out into the open, David placed his life in God's hands to prove his respect.

David asked Saul why he paid attention to slanderers who claimed David was plotting to harm him. He tactfully laid the blame on evil advisers rather than calling Saul a liar directly. This respectful approach gave the king an honorable way to admit his mistake.

David pointed out that the Lord had delivered Saul into his hands inside the cave that very day. His men had urged him to kill the king, but David chose mercy because Saul was the Lord's anointed. His actions proved that he feared God far more than he desired the throne.

Addressing Saul tenderly as 'my father,' David held up the cut piece of robe as physical proof of his innocence. If David were truly a traitor, he would have taken Saul's life instead of just a scrap of cloth. This evidence showed that David had no rebellion in his heart, even while Saul was hunting him down.

David declared that the Lord should be the judge between them and avenge the wrongs done to him. At the same time, David promised that his own hand would never harm Saul. He chose to trust God for justice rather than taking personal revenge.

David quoted an ancient proverb that says evil actions come from evil people. If he were a wicked rebel, he would have committed murder when he had the chance, but his restraint proved he was not wicked. A person's real character is known by what they choose to do.

David asked why the king of Israel was wasting his time chasing someone as lowly as a dead dog or a single flea. These everyday expressions showed that David was completely harmless and posed no threat to the crown. It was beneath the king's royal honor to lead thousands of troops to hunt someone so powerless.

David repeated his prayer that the Lord would examine his cause, act as their judge, and rescue him from Saul. Instead of using violence to escape his suffering, he left his case entirely with God. Believers can rest peacefully when they let God defend them against unfair treatment.

When David finished, Saul recognized his voice, called him 'my son David,' and wept loudly. The king was completely overwhelmed by David's kindness and broken by the shame of his own hatred. Gentle words and mercy can soften even a bitter enemy's heart.

Saul confessed that David was far more righteous than he was, because David had paid back good for evil. The king openly admitted his own wickedness and praised David's upright heart. Genuine goodness has the power to draw out the truth even from those who oppose us.

Saul acknowledged that David had treated him with great mercy in the cave. When the Lord had put Saul at David's mercy, David had refused to kill him. Saul's own words cleared away every false charge that David had ever plotted against him.

Saul pointed out that when a person catches an enemy, he never lets him escape unharmed. Because David had shown such unheard-of mercy, Saul asked the Lord to bless and reward David. Saul knew he had nothing worthy to give, so he asked God to repay David's kindness.

Saul admitted that he now knew for certain that David would become king and that the kingdom would be firmly established in his hands. He had sensed this before, but David's noble character and God's obvious protection made it undeniable. Even Saul recognized that God's plans cannot be stopped.

Saul begged David to swear by the Lord that he would not wipe out Saul's children or erase his family name when he became king. In the ancient world, new rulers often slaughtered the family of the old king to prevent future rebellions. Saul knew David feared God and would keep a sacred promise.

David made the oath to Saul, and Saul went back to his home, while David and his men returned to their mountain refuge. David knew Saul's emotions were unstable, so he wisely kept his distance rather than walking into danger. We should forgive others freely while still using common sense to protect ourselves.
